claims.statement: URE reported 1,636,673 Polish RES micro-installations at the end of 2025, with PV representing 99.9% of them.
Poland's climate ministry reported about 1.63m prosumer installations by April 2026, 99% photovoltaic.

contrary_evidence: The large installed base does not prove that owners have unresolved faults or that installers will outsource monitoring.
OEM portals already monitor many systems, so the control point requires actual dispatch adoption rather than another dashboard.

economics.acquisition_route: Family-business fleet first, then distributors and installer groups with portfolio migration tools
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Illustrative, unvalidated path: 300000 monitored systems at 2.5 PLN monthly plus service revenue could exceed 9m PLN annual revenue; 25% operating margin and 75% ownership could support founder equity above 5m PLN around year 6
economics.founder_time: 2-3 hours/day for data and product, with technicians and customer support delegated
economics.gross_margin_basis: Target blended 50-65%, with high-margin software offset by lower-margin support and dispatch
economics.payback: Unvalidated: 20000 monitored systems plus 200 monthly paid dispatches could repay the pilot within 18 months
economics.pricing: Unvalidated: 1-4 PLN per monitored site monthly plus 10-15% of service or parts transactions
economics.retention_or_repeat: Continuous monitoring subscription and recurring faults, warranties, inspections, and upgrades

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Cross-brand failure signatures, repair outcomes, parts knowledge, and ownership of the dispatch workflow
fingerprint.customer: Polish and Central European small PV installers responsible for legacy customer fleets
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Pilot on the parents' installed base, then installer associations, inverter distributors, and white-label partnerships
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Multi-brand monitoring, triage, customer communication, technician dispatch, warranty evidence, and parts routing
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: Installer pays per monitored site; platform also earns on dispatched service and parts transactions
fingerprint.problem_trigger: An inverter alert, underperformance signal, warranty question, or customer service request occurs

founder_fit: Immediate pilot access through the parents' installation company
Strong fit for anomaly detection and automation
Can start part-time with fieldwork delegated
Builds a data asset from a practical service wedge
risks: Inverter vendors can restrict APIs or bundle their own monitoring
False alarms and missed faults can damage installer relationships
Residential customers may not pay enough to support human support

structure.commercial_archetype: Embedded vertical SaaS with managed service and parts-marketplace revenue
structure.control_point: Installer-authorized telemetry and the default fault-to-dispatch workflow for its installed fleet
structure.critical_dependency: Stable inverter data access and installer willingness to route warranty and service work through the platform

thesis: Give small solar installers a white-label monitoring and warranty triage layer across multiple inverter brands, making it the default route for fault classification, customer messaging, technician dispatch, and parts ordering. The installer retains the customer; the platform gains permissioned telemetry and resolution outcomes across fleets.
title: Installer-Owned PV Fault Dispatch Network
uncertainties: API coverage across the dominant installed inverter brands
Actual unresolved service load within installer portfolios
Installer willingness to pay per site rather than reactively per fault
